executive_assessment.text: The NDC adds Yap/western Chuuk water-risk and tenure/governance detail, while the 2010 report supplies explicitly historical Pohnpei outer-atoll, Chuuk and Yap examples.
Adaptation financing, technical skills and coordination constrain implementation; these institutional findings are not a claim that climate causes violence.

geographic_notes.text: FSM's 2025 NDC identifies drought risk in Yap/western Chuuk and reports limited Chuuk utility water coverage, with Weno the only supplied island, versus much broader Pohnpei utility reach.

Source dated 2025-09 reports: State governments manage land, coast, health, education, water and roads. Yap includes traditional leaders in government; the NDC says tenure matters for adaptation/relocation and can hinder infrastructure.

Source dated 2010 reports: The field report says Pohnpei’s outer atoll islets Pingelap, Mokil, Ant, Pakin, Ngatik, Nukuoro and Kapingamarangi suffered extreme hardship during 2007–08 marine inundation.

Source dated 2010 reports: In Chuuk, Tropical Storm Chataan’s 2002 heavy rain caused over 30 landslides and 47 deaths. The report describes poor roads and unpotable drinking water; high tides and runoff filled potholes on the coastal business-district road.

Source dated 2010 reports: In Yap, 2007–08 surges damaged coastal infrastructure, food and housing; the report says main-island water remained nonpotable and harbor protections were only 30–60 cm above high tide.
